subject: Day 25: chest-incline tummy time
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is 25 days old, inside the 1-month milestone window. The priority this week is logging early head-lifting and watching for the first true social smile, which typically lands between weeks 4 and 6.

Action items
- Run tummy time at 15-20 minutes cumulative today, broken into short bouts after feeds when he is alert. Lay him on your chest at a slight incline to lower the protest in these early weeks. AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Schedule the 1-month well visit if it is not already booked; the window is day 28-35 and you want it on the calendar before the weekend. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/
- Start a feeding and output log now so the pediatrician can plot growth on the WHO curves at the 1-month visit.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Evening fussiness clustering around 5-8pm is the normal witching hour; cradle cap and a single continuously tearing eye with no redness are also benign at this age.
- [monitor] Crying that exceeds 3 hours a day, more than 3 days a week, for 3 weeks fits the Wessel definition of colic; document the pattern but expect a peak near week 6 and resolution by 12-16 weeks.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting paired with weight loss can signal pyloric stenosis; persistent arching and inability to console during feeds warrants a same-day conversation about GERD versus milk-protein intolerance.
- [call now] A rectal temperature of 100.4F or higher, blue color around the lips with crying, or any seizure-like activity is an emergency under 90 days; call the pediatrician or 911 now!

Enrichment opportunities
- Position him on your chest at a slight incline for tummy time so face-tracking motivates the head lift while the angle eases the load on his neck. AAP tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Get face-to-face within 8-12 inches, exaggerate your expression, and hold it; the directed social smile he is working toward emerges weeks 4-6. AAP movement birth to three months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Begin a daily 10-15 minute read-aloud with a rotating 3-5 board-book set such as Black on White and Brown Bear, Brown Bear; the rhythm and cadence are the active ingredients now. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; bring the feeding and output log
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; vaccines HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1
- Day 57-72: post-2-month-vaccine window; expect 24-48h of fussiness, drowsiness, and low-grade fever

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
